optionalAuth.title: Inicio de sesión y acceso remoto
optionalAuth.body:
Ya puedes activar la autenticación opcional en la config-api.

Con el login (Ajustes → Seguridad, o AUTH_ENABLED=true), el panel pide correo + contraseña (la primera visita crea el admin). Las API y acciones de contenedores quedan bloqueadas sin sesión — mucho más seguro para usarlo fuera de casa con Nginx Proxy Manager, Caddy, Traefik, etc. por HTTPS.

Sigue siendo zero-config por defecto: la auth está apagada hasta que la actives. No publiques el puerto 8086 en Internet sin auth.

Consulta el changelog. Google / Microsoft / passkeys vienen después.

configApiRequired.title: Se requiere actualizar la config-api
configApiRequired.body:
Esta versión del panel necesita hobbithole-config-api en la misma versión.

Las instalaciones tempranas a veces solo tenían la imagen del dashboard. Sin config-api pierdes sync multi-dispositivo, widgets, temas, fondos y el clima.

docker pull piggyoriginal/hobbithole-config-api:latest
Luego reinicia el servicio config-api (compose en Docker Hub / GitHub).

help.title: 📚 Ayuda y consejos
help.intro: Los campos se mantienen cortos. Aquí están las respuestas largas — abre un tema o busca.

icons.title: App icons (slug, URL, or upload)
icons.body:
When adding/editing an app you can set the icon in three ways:

  • Slug — name from the dashboard-icons library (e.g. sonarr, jellyfin), loaded from a CDN.
  • URL — paste a direct link to PNG, SVG, GIF, or WebP. Nothing is stored locally; great for project logos (e.g. Spotweb).
  • Upload (📁) — file is stored as a data URL in your config (uses more storage).

GitHub tip: use raw.githubusercontent.com/…, not the blob page. Links with /blob/ or ?raw=true are rewritten automatically.

If a slug is missing from the library you see initials (DiceBear) until you pick a URL or upload.

tiles.title: Tiles & app URLs
tiles.body:
Each tile is a link (name + icon + URL). Bare IPs/ports are fine — http:// is added if no scheme is present.

  • ⋯ on a tile: edit, pin, delete, container start/stop/restart (when Docker is available).
  • Categories can collapse and reorder under Settings → Apps.
  • Per-app widgets (stats) are configured on the tile.

benchmark.title: System benchmark (p95 CPU/RAM)
benchmark.body:
Settings → System Benchmark runs ~5 minutes across all running Docker containers (not tiles or external bookmarks).

  • Results are CSVs on the host and show as p95 CPU/RAM on tiles.
  • Tile names match container names after normalizing (strip spaces, -, _). Example: tile Immich Server ↔ container immich_server.
  • Deliberately different names (e.g. Jellyfin Fork vs jellyfin) will not match.
  • New containers appear only after a new run.

auth.title: Login & security
auth.body:
Login is optional (off by default). Enable it under Settings → Security if you reach the dashboard remotely via a reverse proxy.

  • Disabling does not delete accounts — data stays in data/auth/.
  • Re-enabling uses the same email + password (no first-run again) when users already exist.
  • Compose can force policy with AUTH_ENABLED=true|false (UI toggle locked).

Without login: do not expose port 8086 to the internet.

widgets.title: Home widgets
widgets.body:
Add widgets on the home layout (weather, downloads, media, Proxmox, …). Configure API keys and URLs per widget in Settings or on the tile.

  • Some widgets need extra compose setup (USB eject, Watchtower HTTP API).
  • Empty home? Use “add your first widget” or Edit Home.

wallpapers.title: Backgrounds & themes
wallpapers.body:
Appearance: accent color, transparency, theme engine, and wallpapers.

  • Static — one image (file via config-api, not a giant data URL in config).
  • Dynamic — up to 5 time-of-day slots.
  • Live — short video background (max ~20 MB).

Files live under the config-api wallpapers path so every device matches.

docker.title: Docker: scan, start/stop
docker.body:
The dashboard can list containers and start/stop/restart them via the config-api.

  • Scan suggests tiles; matching uses port and/or container name.
  • Host-network or stopped containers may have empty port lists — name matching covers that.
  • Not every container needs a tile; external bookmarks are not part of the benchmark.

home.title: Home / canvas editing
home.body:
Home layout (canvas) lets you arrange blocks and widgets. Enable Edit Home to drag and resize.

  • Preference is stored on the server (cross-device).
  • Command palette / search actions cover quick navigation.

status.title: Status dot: Docker first, else URL
status.body:
Green/red does not always mean “website opens”.

  • Docker match — if the tile maps to a container (port, name, or Docker container name), the dot follows container state: running = green, else red. Tooltip shows the container name.
  • URL ping — no Docker match → the browser probes the tile URL (as before). Localhost-only ports (e.g. CrowdSec LAPI on 127.0.0.1) looked “down” while the container was fine.

Compact service tile: short row with name, status dot, and p95 RAM (no large icon). Great for infra without a web UI. Toggle when editing an app.

Stacking: mark several apps as compact service tiles and drag them under each other in Apps. Consecutive compact tiles form a vertical stack. Reorder chips inside the stack, or pull one out next to the large app cards.

updates.title: Updates from Docker Hub
updates.body:
The footer can show a quiet Update badge when Docker Hub has a newer release tag than this install.

  • Always pull both hobbithole-dashboard and hobbithole-config-api to the same version — mixed tags break sync, auth, and widgets.
  • If Hub lists different newest tags for the two images, the Help panel warns you and points at the newer tag for both.
  • Watchtower may refresh digests for :latest; this badge is about a newer version tag (e.g. 1.10.1 → 1.10.2).
  • Dismiss hides the badge until an even newer Hub tag appears.
